# difficulty

> A compiled language for AI agents and humans: C-like syntax, Python-like simplicity,
> one way to write each thing, no silent fallbacks, diagnostics that say how to fix them.
> This file covers parts 1 ("Hallo, nativ") and 2a (values, methods). The binding description
> is docs/spec.md; error codes are rule numbers (R1–R31) or lexical/syntax codes (L, S).

## Tools

```
dif check [--json] main.dif    # syntax, names, types; one JSON object per line with --json
dif run main.dif               # compile via C11 and run
dif build main.dif -o prog     # native program (needs cc, gcc or clang; or set CC)
```

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 diagnostics, 2 usage error or a panic of the program.
A diagnostic: `main.dif:3:11: error[R9]: condition is int, not bool` plus `hint: …`.
Columns count characters. Each mistake gives exactly one diagnostic; fix the first, rerun.

## A program

```dif
const int LIMIT = 10

int square(int n) {
    return n * n
}

void main() {
    int total = 0
    for int i in range(1, LIMIT) {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            continue
        }
        total += square(i)
    }
    print("sum of odd squares below {LIMIT}: {total}")
}
```

- A program is functions and `const` declarations, in any order; it starts in `void main()`.
- Statements only inside functions. No global variables, only global `const`.

## Rules of part 1

**Lines.** A statement ends at the end of its line. No `;`. A line continues when it ends
with a binary operator, `=`, an assignment operator or `,`, inside `( )` and `[ ]`,
or when the next line starts with `.`. Two statements on one line: R3.

**Blocks.** Always `{ }`, the `{` on the line of its header, `} else {` on one line.
No parentheses needed around conditions. `else if`, never `elif`.

**Declarations name their type first** and always have a value (R2):
`int n = 0`, `bool done = false`, `str name = "dif"`, `const int K = 3`.
Function: `int add(int a, int b) { … }`; no return value: `void`.
Loop variables too: `for int i in range(n)`.

**Names (R4).** A name lives until the end of its block, including inner blocks, and is
never declared again there (no shadowing, also not as parameter or loop variable).
Sibling blocks may reuse a name. `const` is never assigned. Predefined names
(`print range int bool str` …) and keywords cannot be names; `ok`, `err`, `none`,
`some`, `test` are reserved. Names use ASCII letters, digits and `_`.

**Types (R8).** `int` (64 bit), `bool`, `str`, `void`. Types never mix:
`"a" + 1` is an error; build text with interpolation `"{a}{b}"`.

| operator | operands | result |
|---|---|---|
| `+ - * / %` `+% -% *%` `& \| ^ << >>` | int, int | int |
| `-x` `~x` | int | int |
| `+` | str, str | str |
| `== !=` | same type | bool |
| `< <= > >=` | int or str (both the same) | bool |
| `&& \|\| !` | bool | bool (R9) |

**Conditions are bool (R9).** `while n {` is an error; write `while n != 0 {`.

**Precedence**, weakest first: `??` · `||` · `&&` · comparisons · `|` · `^` · `&` ·
shifts · `+ -` · `* / %` · unary `- ! ~` · call/index/field. Bit operators bind tighter
than comparisons: `x & 1 == 0` means `(x & 1) == 0`.
Not allowed: chains `a < b < c` (S2, write `a < b && b < c`) and `&&` mixed with `||`
without parentheses (S3).

**Loops (R11).** `for int i in range(n)` (0 … n-1), `for int i in range(a, b)` (a … b-1),
bounds evaluated once; `while cond`; `break`, `continue` only inside loops.
`range` only appears as the source of a `for`.

**Results are used (R13).** A call of a function that returns a value, used as a
statement, is an error; use the value or discard it explicitly: `_ = f(x)`.
`print(x)` returns nothing and is a statement.

**Numbers (R29, R14).** Overflow of `+ - *` and unary `-` aborts; `+% -% *%` wrap
modulo 2^64. `/` rounds toward 0, `%` has the sign of the dividend (`-7 / 2 == -3`,
`-7 % 3 == -1`). Division by 0 and `INT_MIN / -1` abort; `INT_MIN % -1` is 0.
Shifts take 0 … 63 places, `>>` keeps the sign. Operands and arguments are evaluated
left to right. Literals: `1_000`, `0xff`, `0b1010`; no leading zeros, no `0X`.
Expressions of literals and `const` are computed exactly at compile time; only the
result must fit (`-9223372036854775808` is fine); a certain abort there (`1 / 0`) is R14.

**Text.** `"…"` on one line. Escapes `\n \t \r \\ \" \{ \} \0 \u{1F600}`.
`{expr}` inserts any int, bool or str; no strings or braces inside `{ }`;
a literal brace is `\{` or `\}`. `print(x)` writes `x` and a newline.

**Abort.** A programming error stops the program with
`panic: integer overflow in + (main.dif:3:15)` on stderr and exit code 2.

```dif snippet
int big = 9223372036854775807
print(big +% 1)
print(-7 / 2)
print(1 << 62)
str s = "a" + "b"
bool same = s == "ab"
print("{s} {same}")
```

```dif panic "division by zero"
int z = 0
print(10 / z)
```

## Part 2a: values, methods, `mut`, `switch`

```dif
struct Point {
    int x
    int y = 0
}

enum Shape {
    Square(int side)
    Rect(int w, int h)
    Dot
}

Point Point.moved(int dx) {
    Point q = self
    q.x += dx
    return q
}

void Point.scale(int k) {
    self.x *= k
    self.y *= k
}

void shift(mut Point p, int dx) {
    p.x += dx
}

int area(Shape s) {
    switch s {
    case Shape.Square(int side):
        return side * side
    case Shape.Rect(int w, _):
        return w
    case Shape.Dot:
        return 0
    }
}

void main() {
    Point a = Point{x: 1, y: 2}
    Point b = a
    shift(mut b, 5)
    b.scale(2)
    int n = if b.x > 10 { area(Shape.Square(3)) } else { 0 }
    print("{a} {b} {b.moved(1)} {n} {Shape.Rect(3, 4)}")
}
```

Output: `Point{x: 1, y: 2} Point{x: 12, y: 4} Point{x: 13, y: 4} 9 Shape.Rect(3, 4)`

- **`struct` (R5).** One field per line, optional default (`int y = 0`, constants and
  effect-free calls only, evaluated at every literal that omits the field). A literal
  names every field without default, in any order, evaluated left to right:
  `Point{x: 1}`. Assignment, parameters and return copy the value. A type cannot
  contain itself.
- **`enum` (R5).** `enum Seat { Free, Taken }`; variants may carry values
  (`NoSuchSeat(int row, int seat)`). Always written with the type: `Seat.Free`,
  `BookErr.NoSuchSeat(3, 5)`. Values are read only through `switch`.
- **`mut` (R6).** A function that changes an argument takes it as `mut T p` and the
  caller writes `mut`: `shift(mut b, 5)`. `mut` takes variables, fields (`mut s.player`).
  A `mut` parameter that is never changed, a change that is never read afterwards (also
  to a copy: a parameter without `mut`) and one place passed changeable twice in a call
  are R6. An argument without `mut` that reads the same place sees the value from
  before the call.
- **Methods (R7).** `R Type.name(params)`; `self` is the place before the dot and may
  be changed. `a.scale(2)` needs a variable or field when the method changes `self`;
  methods that only read work on any expression: `fresh().total()`. No `mut` at the call.
- **`switch` (R10).** Over `int`, `str` or `enum`; values are literals, `const` names or
  `E.V`; `case 1, 2:` lists values; bindings `case E.V(int w, _):` (one value per
  entry, `_` skips). No fall-through; `continue` and `return` work inside, `break` is not
  used directly in a `switch`. Every variant is handled or there is a `default`; over
  `int`/`str` `default` is required. Statements of a case start on the next line.
- **`if` as a value (R15).** `str s = if n < 0 { "neg" } else { "pos" }`; `else` is
  required, each branch ends with an expression (statements may come before it), only the
  chosen branch runs, all branches have one type.
- **Equality and text (R28).** `==` compares structs field by field and enums by variant
  and values; text looks like the literal, `str` inside is quoted:
  `Person{name: "Ada", age: 36}`, `BookErr.NoSuchSeat(3, 5)`. `<` does not exist for them.

```dif error R6
struct Point {
    int x
    int y
}

void shift(mut Point p, int dx) {
    p.x += dx
}

void main() {
    Point b = Point{x: 1, y: 2}
    shift(b, 5)
    print(b)
}
```

## Habits from other languages and their fixes

| written | code | write instead |
|---|---|---|
| `var x = 5`, `let x = 5`, `auto x = 5` | R2 | `int x = 5` |
| `def f():`, `fn f(a: int) -> int`, `function f()` | R2 | `int f(int a) { … }` |
| `x: int` in parameters, `-> int` | R2 | `int f(int x) {` |
| `for i in range(10)` | R2 | `for int i in range(10)` |
| `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)` | R11 | `for int i in range(n)` |
| `elif`, `elsif` | R3 | `} else if … {` |
| `{` on the next line | R3 | `if x > 0 {` |
| `if x > 0 print(x)` | R3 | `if x > 0 { print(x) }` on separate lines |
| `x = 1;` | L3 | `x = 1` |
| `i++`, `--i` | L7 | `i += 1`, `i -= 1` |
| `/* … */` | L2 | `// …` |
| `010` | L8 | `10` |
| `if x = 1 {` | S1 | `if x == 1 {` |
| `while n {` | R9 | `while n != 0 {` |
| `"n = " + n` | R8 | `"n = {n}"` |
| `f(x)` result unused | R13 | `int y = f(x)` or `_ = f(x)` |
| `int n` without value | R2 | `int n = 0` |
| `shift(b, 5)` when `shift` takes `mut` | R6 | `shift(mut b, 5)` |
| `case Free:` in a `switch` over an enum | R10 | `case Seat.Free:` |
| assignment to an undeclared name | R2 | declare it: `int x = …` |
| `void main(void)` | S1 | `void main()` |

```dif error R2
void main() {
    var x = 5
    print(x)
}
```

```dif error R13
int square(int n) {
    return n * n
}

void main() {
    square(3)
}
```

## Limits

Nesting deeper than 256 levels or more than 1024 operators in one expression is S1;
a chain of more than 256 `const` using each other is R4. Split the code.

## Not yet

Floating point and other number types, lists, maps, `T!E`, `?T`, `try`, `??`, modules,
tests, C import, handles and sharing. They follow in later parts (see PLAN.md); using
them gives an error that says so.
